newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:

* President Clinton in his State of the Union Message called education the top priority of his second term and urged Congress to pass a balanced budget without amending the Constitution, but did not present any major federal spending initiatives.

* In the Republican reply to the president's State of the Union Message, Rep. J.C. Watts of Oklahoma outlined an agenda based less on policy than inner personal strength, criticizing Clinton's reliance on government to solve racial problems.
* A 12-member, largely white civil jury ruled after 16 hours of deliberations that O.J. Simpson is responsible for the killings of his ex-wife Nicole Simpson and Ronald Goldman.

* After 77 days of street protests and intense diplomatic pressure, Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic said he would reverse his decision to annul the November elections in which the opposition won in 14 of Serbia's 19 largest cities.
* Two Israeli helicopters taking soldiers to Lebanon collided over the northern Galilee, killing all 73 men on board.

* New U.S. Secretery of State Madeleine Albright says she is grateful for her parents' painful decision to convert from Judaism to Catholicism in between the two World Wars, and called them "the bravest people alive."
